CORE EXPLANATION

Vec<T> is a growable array, String stores UTF-8 text, and HashMap stores key-value pairs. Consider bounds and ownership; iteration is often clearer than indexing.

Vec<T> is a growable list, HashMap<K,V> maps keys to values, and HashSet<T> stores unique values; arrays have fixed length. Collections own their elements, so insertion and borrowing follow ownership rules. `get()` returns Option for a missing index, while direct indexing may panic. Choose based on access patterns and measure realistic workloads.
